nativeStates.textBox: Keyboard focus within: Focus border. Minimum height: 36 DIP. TechnicalText inherits the themed TextBox style and adds Consolas diagnostics typography.
nativeStates.comboBox: Keyboard focus within: 2 DIP Focus outline. Disabled opacity: 0.55.
nativeStates.navigation: Selected: Selection fill and semibold text. Hover: Border stroke. Keyboard focus within: Focus stroke.
nativeStates.slider: Keyboard focus: 1 DIP Focus outline. Disabled opacity: 0.5.
nativeStates.profileCard: Selected card uses ProfileSelection tint, Accent border and Editing badge; active keyboard profile is shown separately.
nativeStates.deviceKey: Keymap only: four native ListBox regions support mouse selection and keyboard navigation. Hover: KeyHover fill and Focus outline. Selected: KeySelection fill and Accent outline. Keyboard focus within: OnAccent inner ring and Focus outer outline. Home and Device remain noninteractive.
nativeStates.shortcutCapture: Selection panel replaces Record/Clear while recording and shows instructions, held modifiers and explicit Cancel. Escape is captured as a key. Changing key/profile/page, window deactivation and closure cancel. Manual HID builder offers primary keys, left modifiers and nested right-side variants; Windows-intercepted shortcuts can be built manually.
nativeStates.keymapFeedback: Route notices and failed-or-uncertain write recovery render immediately below the inspector title through the existing polite live region. Feedback derives failure from exact-current-key/value PhysicalState, so later edits do not inherit stale failure. Failed draft is retained; replay evidence is not a physical failure observation.
nativeStates.bleFeedback: Inline Danger errors and actionable recovery copy. A transport-prefixed localized fresh/stale label uses local date/time and offset in Focus. One transport-owned observation/freshness snapshot per refresh supplies body and header; Diagnostics shows its session. Switching never imports telemetry from the previous transport. The five-second UI timer reevaluates the 60-second age limit without telemetry polling; disconnect also makes observations stale. Missing data remains Unknown. Stale battery retains a written body qualifier; stale physical mode and confirmation become Unknown.
nativeStates.bleActions: Transport selection requires idle Real mode and releases the previous session before ownership. Discovery requires idle, non-live Real mode. Bluetooth Connect/Reconnect require a selection; saved startup/loss each permit one bounded burst of at most two attempts. USB selection/Find enumerate metadata only; Connect/Reconnect require one positively identified HID candidate and remain disabled when unavailable or ambiguous. USB never auto-connects or falls back. Refresh requires idle live mode. Disconnect cancels recovery/releases the session and is also available while work or the USB reader is active. Forget is Bluetooth-only and clears saved selection while retaining local configuration.
nativeStates.bleDiagnostics: Localized summary and transport rows retain device/battery/firmware/capabilities and freshness. Bluetooth shows adapter/session/subscription; USB shows source/session/reader, compatibility, queries and errors. Collapsed Advanced keeps Bluetooth GATT details or USB collection/usage, sizes/report policy, native input/output reports, frame, native write result and timing. CatalogLabel selects GATT or localized Discovered HID interfaces; USB candidate catalog and copied diagnostics redact hardware identities. Copy confirms success in its label. Catalog/history use selectable wrapping TechnicalText.
nativeStates.shellBackend: Profiles opens in Real. Header shows connection/fresh battery and Apply on Keymap only. Editing and active keyboard profile are separate. Global activation errors remain visible across pages with both contexts and recovery to Profiles. No Real Synced or full-profile write.
nativeStates.advancedControls: Shared Expander and CheckBox styles bind Foreground to DynamicResource TextPrimary. Settings Advanced reveals Developer mode; the backend selector appears only when enabled. Turning Developer mode off restores Real. BLE errors never silently select Mock.
nativeStates.devicePicker: Explicit Bluetooth/USB buttons use Selection fill and Accent border for the selected transport. Bluetooth native ListBox shows recognizable names and Bluetooth subtitle without raw Windows IDs. USB shows the localized neutral AhaKey USB device name and identified/unavailable/ambiguous guidance, never an inferred Bluetooth name/model. Metadata Find is separate from explicit Connect.
nativeStates.integrationRows: Rows show readiness, service state, saved feedback preference and activity separately, with contextual actions, Details and More actions. Details holds individual installation/configuration/enablement/trust/compatibility evidence. Ready does not mean service running. In-place refresh preserves focus and review.
nativeStates.integrationDetails: Opening Details positions the inline section through the outer ScrollViewer and focuses Close details; closing returns focus and visibility to the initiating button. The section shows sanitized selectable configuration path, native last event, trust explanation and wrapped Install/Configure/Repair/Remove actions. Install adds hooks, not the assistant. Configure actions require installed compatible non-Kimi evidence and idle state. Native Codex trust/enablement are separate decisions and are not automatically changed by Studio.
nativeStates.integrationPreview: Explicit review precedes Apply: affected native event, owned-entry count before/after, sanitized command, matcher, timeout, file path, purpose and pre/post SHA-256. No-change plans display written feedback and disable Apply. PrimaryButton applies reviewed changes; Cancel discards the plan. Receipt shows a localized result and sanitized backup directory. Unrelated configuration stays outside the preview and ownership boundary.
nativeStates.integrationFeedback: Service starts explicitly or after persisted autostart opt-in on launch. Written running/stopped status stays separate from Ready; metadata diagnostics remains collapsed. Stop attempts Off for its own accepted matching-session feedback without erasing preference.
nativeStates.integrationApproval: Hardware AUTO remains initially off and session-only inside collapsed approvals. Saved service autostart and lighting preference remain independent. Manual approval retains event context, deadline and explicit Deny/Allow; unavailable evidence never implies consent. Event-driven Display is unavailable; explicit profile activation has a separate accepted runtime path.
nativeStates.physicalKeyReview: Valid Real K2–K4 Apply remains actionable over BLE while no key write/USB operation runs. Missing, ambiguous or unaccepted USB sends no write and preserves BLE/draft. One exact private USB candidate takes exclusive ownership, validates live identity/firmware and confirms the minimal selected-key plan with no-backup/global-save consequences, releases USB and restores eligible prior BLE once without write retry. Exact USB device/firmware/target/value receipts retain Written to AhaKey (USB); never readback or Synced. Optional focused physical Test requires matching receipt/profile/session.
nativeStates.lighting: Normal view leads with integration, saved On/Off preference and live-route availability. Missing accepted route offers direct Connect USB. USB and separately command-tested/user-observed BLE permit only 00/01 for their own exact private identity/firmware. USB key/Display evidence never transfers to BLE. Numeric Preview, brightness, nine-event mapping and counters remain collapsed in Advanced.
nativeStates.physicalFeedback: Saved per-profile/integration opt-in, initially off for new settings; reconnect/restart preserves the choice. Actual output requires matching accepted device/firmware/effects and live physical profile. Failure pauses the failed connection without clearing preference; reconnect or off/on permits recovery. Hardware AUTO remains independent and session-only.
nativeStates.displayPlanner: Imported source cache/name/target/Fit-Crop persist. Physical Upload is one non-GIF frame, Codex Default slot 9, attested AD1E USB firmware 1.0 active mode 2. Unsupported target/content stays disabled. Missing connection/mode redirects to Device without writing. Concise Cancel / Replace image protects replacement; exact technical detail and export stay in collapsed Advanced. Fresh 83 preflight and separate user image inspection remain required.
nativeStates.parentScroll: Integrations PreviewMouseWheel scrolls the parent shell ScrollViewer over child controls; fixed sidebar/header and existing vertical layout remain.
nativeStates.phase6Current:
- **Phase 6.1 route and receipt states:** normal Apply discovers one exact privately accepted USB candidate before opening it, acquires exclusive ownership, validates the live USB identity/firmware and confirms device/profile/key, shortcut/label and no-backup/global-save consequences. It releases USB and restores the previous BLE connection only while the operation still owns that session/selection and no explicit disconnect intervened; writes never retry. Missing, ambiguous or unaccepted USB sends no write and preserves BLE/draft. An exact USB receipt matching device, firmware, target and value shows Written to AhaKey (USB) after BLE restoration. Only a baseline without that matching receipt reports write status unavailable. This supersedes Phase 6's blanket unavailable state on BLE, without claiming readback or Synced. Test key remains optional; focused matching input must belong to the same live session/profile and unchanged receipt before behavior is verified.
- **Phase 6 persisted preferences:** feedback and service autostart default off in new settings and survive restart once explicitly enabled. Codex simple mapping uses 01 for UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse and 00 for Stop/TaskCompleted/SessionEnd/PermissionRequest; unmapped events send nothing. Actual output remains gated by accepted identity/firmware/effects and matching live profile. Failure pauses a connection without deleting the preference; stopping service attempts Off for its own matching-session output. Hardware AUTO remains separate and session-only.
- **Phase 6 Display source and recovery:** imported source cache, original name, target and Fit/Crop survive profile changes/restart. One non-GIF frame for Codex / Default / slot 9 remains the only accepted physical target. Unsupported targets/content disable Upload with an explanation. A supported prepared image lacking eligible connection/mode sends nothing and opens Device with guidance. Concise Cancel / Replace image protects replacement; exact technical details remain available in collapsed Advanced.
- **Phase 6 readiness and profile activation:** Ready derives from installed/configured/enabled/compatible evidence and trusted or not-required trust; service running is separate. Optional persisted activation, initially off, lets explicit profile selection/Activate now issue accepted 92 and verify 00. Failures remain visible globally with recovery to Profiles; no automatic key rewriting occurs.

narrative.overview:
Phase 6.1 current-state clarification (source-derived, superseding earlier Phase 6 product-completion and route-state claims): this is a focused refinement of the established native WPF Operate world; all visual tokens remain unchanged. The user accepted Phase 6 backend capabilities but rejected its normal product flow: BLE hid key Apply and left accepted lighting unusable, while About and the footer disagreed. That firsthand rejection supersedes the earlier completion claim without invalidating its individually recorded evidence.

Normal K2–K4 Apply stays actionable for a valid edit while using BLE. Missing USB produces near-title Connect USB guidance; the reviewed exact private USB route temporarily owns the device, performs the minimal selected-key write, releases USB and restores the prior BLE connection when eligible. An exact matching receipt remains explicitly Written to AhaKey (USB), never Synced or BLE readback. Failed-or-uncertain key writes retain the draft and expose recovery immediately under the inspector title through the existing polite live region; `Feedback` derives this from the exact-current-key/value `PhysicalState`, so a later edit does not inherit stale failure text. K1 stays locked.

Lighting keeps the saved preference separate from route availability and provides a direct Connect USB recovery action when no accepted route is live. Separate successful trial commands and user-observed on/off states now accept BLE runtime 00/01 only for the exact privately attested device and firmware; USB key/Display capability and other effects do not transfer. Footer, About, Diagnostics, copied exports and startup/support logs use assembly-derived `AppVersionService` for 2.0.0-alpha.6.1, with build/revision labeled separately. Profiles still distinguishes Editing from the active keyboard profile and preserves global activation recovery.

The [Phase 6.1 bounded review](../../docs/studio2-phase61/ui-review.md) returns **ship only for the resolved near-title key-write failure finding**. Its initial 36-capture offline review and three-image finding check are software UI evidence, not a renewed whole-surface audit. The [normal-app evidence](../../docs/studio2-phase61/physical-acceptance.md) records USB write ACKs, BLE restoration and actual Codex event/ACK traffic separately from the [user-observed isolated BLE trial](../../docs/studio2-phase61/ble-rgb-result.md). Final physical K2 and normal Codex visual confirmations remain pending; full Phase 6.1 product acceptance is not claimed. See [direction](../../docs/studio2-phase61/ui-direction.md) and [capability decisions](../../docs/studio2-phase61/capability-gating.md). Historical reviews below retain their original scope; this documentation refresh performs no new visual or hardware check.

The approved brief defines a restrained native Windows utility with persistent navigation, an always-visible profile selector, compact connection feedback, and clear local-configuration provenance. Historically, Phase 5 extended the accepted WPF Operate design with exact-scope static Display upload, factual locked-K1 status, and accepted live RGB feedback; reviewed selected-key writes and local image planning remain. Earlier Phase 3.4 added explicit read-only USB alongside Bluetooth; normal connection telemetry retains that boundary. The photo-based key editor, dedicated inspector, and existing visual language remain intact; this is an extension of the established task-oriented design, not a new visual direction.

Preserve four stable profile IDs (0–3), runtime EN/RU/ZH localization, and System/Light/Dark theme choices. Normal startup opens Profiles in Real mode, with System language/theme on first run and a Connect AhaKey entry point. Mock is available through Settings → Advanced → Developer mode and remains explicitly labeled Simulation when selected. Errors never silently select Mock. Real mode distinguishes unavailable full-profile writes/readback from accepted selected-key writes, preserving local-configuration provenance; connection and fresh telemetry never imply synchronization. Local shortcut capture remains available in either mode. The inspector Test button, full-profile write and configuration readback belong only to Mock; an accepted selected-key write enables a separate optional Test key action with focused physical observation.

The token snapshot above comes from `Themes/Light.xaml`, `Themes/Dark.xaml`, `Themes/Controls.xaml`, `Themes/Typography.xaml`, and the native views. Dimensions are WPF device-independent pixels (DIP), not measured monitor pixels. The companion `.impeccable/design.json` records native behavior outside the portable token schema.

Historical review, recorded 2026-09-20: the [Phase 3.3 review](../../docs/studio2-phase33/ui-review.md) closes its two material findings after correction `8ed3bc4`: Dark Advanced/developer text and consistent stale-battery presentation. This is a finding-level visual verdict, not a new whole-surface or hardware certification. The [alpha handoff](../../docs/studio2-phase33/alpha-handoff.md) separates actual published-app screenshots, software checks, and user-approved AD1E physical acceptance; these results are not new AE1E acceptance. Earlier first-run/picker and powered-off captures are identified there. No HTML/CSS detector applies to native WPF.

The [Phase 3.4 review](../../docs/studio2-phase34/ui-review.md) returns **ship** for the scoped Device/Diagnostics extension at `2d3c906`. The [USB handoff](../../docs/studio2-phase34/usb-handoff.md) separates 14 software-only 1024-DIP captures (EN/RU/ZH × Light/Dark Device and Diagnostics, plus identified/ambiguous USB) from eight physical AD1E native-window captures at `03cb010`. The physical Advanced image retains the former GATT heading; final source uses the transport-specific HID heading. These are dated evidence boundaries, not a new physical acceptance run or AE1E certification. Screenshot review does not establish actual monitor-DPI, high-contrast, or screen-reader acceptance.

The built contract is explicit transport choice and truthful telemetry within the existing flat native WPF utility: identify, connect, then inspect. Device starts with transport choice and actions, followed by timestamped telemetry; the header shows selected-key Apply on Keymap in Real mode and hides full-profile Write elsewhere. This narrow Operate extension preserves the existing blue accent, semantic Light/Dark surfaces, Segoe UI, and shell without a new visual identity, comp, or token change.

Historically, Phase 4A extended that incumbent system with the built Integrations workspace and manual approval window. Four assistant rows separate installation, configuration, enablement, trust, compatibility, and activity; service status remains independent. Configuration changes require a concrete owned-change preview and explicit Apply. That host integration extension did not enable physical configuration, task-state, lighting, display or firmware output. Phase 4B adds only the separately gated controls described below. The [surface brief](../../docs/studio2-phase4a/surface-brief.md) and [source contract](../../docs/studio2-phase4a/source-contract.md) define the scope without introducing new tokens or a new visual identity.

The [Phase 4A review](../../docs/studio2-phase4a/ui-review.md) returns **ship** only for three corrected findings: concrete configuration consent, keyboard focus retained across updates, and Details reveal/return. Captures in `.impeccable/review/phase4a/` distinguish offline EN/RU/ZH × Light/Dark fixtures and interaction/error examples from installed-host and actual Codex event evidence. Fixture versions, trust states, Simulation header, and empty profile selector are not installed-host facts. The verdict is not whole-surface, screen-reader, actual-monitor DPI, Windows high-contrast, physical telemetry, or BLE/USB acceptance. Earlier phase evidence above retains its original scope.

Historically, Phase 4B kept that Operate identity and the existing tokens. Keymap adds an exact selected-key command preview and distinct pending, ACK-accepted, behavior-verified and indeterminate states. Lighting separates the nine local event mappings, explicit runtime preview and session-only per-profile/per-integration physical feedback. At that checkpoint Display imported and previewed local images/GIFs and exported a technical plan with a visible physical NO-GO; no upload action existed. Phase 5 adds only the accepted static scope described below.

Physical evidence at the Phase 4B completion checkpoint was narrow: AD1E USB K2 Ctrl+Enter was ACK-accepted and user behavior-verified, without configuration readback. The separately approved completion trial on the same USB identity and firmware 1.0 added user-observed acceptance for RGB `91 01` and Off `91 00` only. Numeric Effect 01 avoids an unproved marketing name; Off is not restoration of unknown previous output. Acceptance binds to the connected device/path, transport and firmware; USB evidence does not enable BLE or AE1E. Offline accepted-device fixtures remain software UI evidence. [Completion physical evidence](../../docs/studio2-phase4b-completion/physical-acceptance.md) carries the ledger and separate visual confirmation.

The [Phase 4B direction](../../docs/studio2-phase4b/ui-direction.md) and [review](../../docs/studio2-phase4b/ui-review.md) describe this code-led extension. The [final verdict](../../docs/studio2-phase4b/ui-verdict.md) returns **ship** for its two resolved findings only: current feedback failure/recovery takes precedence over historical preview messages, and EN/RU/ZH Device/header guidance distinguishes full-profile restrictions from accepted selected-key writes. The reviewer inspected eight original and four additional offline captures; no new review or hardware acceptance is asserted here. The waiting-only Key Test image does not demonstrate a physical keystroke. Native dialogs, full keyboard traversal, screen readers, actual-monitor DPI and Windows high contrast retain the review's stated coverage limits. That checkpoint preceded the separately recorded RGB visual acceptance; its original review scope remains unchanged.

The completion extension preserves the incumbent Operate identity, blue Light/Dark tokens, Segoe UI, supplied hardware photograph, EN/RU/ZH and 1024-DIP minimum-width layout. It adds manual shortcut construction, direct contextual integration actions, standalone numeric RGB preview, parent mouse-wheel handling and Fit/Crop with RGB565 preview. The fresh completion review returned **ship**, with no material fixes, for the supplied native UI evidence. Nine captures live in `.impeccable/review/phase4b-completion/`; their offline device, version, trust and event states do not prove hardware or installed-host behavior. This documentation inspected source and four representative captures. No comp or HTML/CSS detector applies; screenshot review does not certify physical output, screen readers, actual monitor DPI or high contrast.

Phase 5 preserves the same code-led native Operate world, blue/Segoe UI, supplied assets, semantic Light/Dark resources and EN/RU/ZH. Display makes the target, local import/Fit/Crop, quantized preview and static-upload entry visible before expanded technical details. Only the privately attested AD1E USB firmware 1.0 profile-2 Default slot-9 route is enabled; every upload requires destructive exact-range/hash review. K1 states that F19 was not observed despite ACKs and F18 restoration was observed, and stays locked. Lighting distinguishes local mappings, per-profile/integration opt-in, connection reset and received/suppressed/operation/ACK counters. See the [Phase 5 direction](../../docs/studio2-phase5/ui-direction.md), [handoff](../../docs/studio2-phase5/handoff.md) and separate K1/RGB/Display physical records linked there.

The [Phase 5 finish review](../../docs/studio2-phase5/ui-review.md) returns **ship** after its one English-text finding was corrected. The final [36 offline captures](../../docs/studio2-phase5/evidence/ui) cover static Display, Lighting, feedback on/off, locked K1 and overwrite confirmation across EN/RU/ZH and Light/Dark. Main views use the reviewed 1024-DIP layout; the dialog is separate and feedback views are scrolled. The initial full matrix review and bounded final finding check do not constitute a second whole-surface or hardware audit. No HTML/CSS detector ran for native WPF. Keyboard traversal, screen readers, actual monitor DPI, Windows high contrast, smaller dialog sizes and live error/loading interaction retain the stated coverage limits.

rules.name: The Semantic Resource Rule
rules.body: Bind themed brushes through `DynamicResource`; keep brush values in the two theme dictionaries. Shared Expander and CheckBox styles bind `Foreground` to `TextPrimary`, including Settings Developer mode and Diagnostics Advanced. System selects a supported theme rather than defining a third palette.

rules.name: The Written Status Rule
rules.body: Pair state color with localized text. Distinguish connection, synchronization, and settings or operation errors.

dos: **Do** preserve the fixed sidebar, persistent profile/connection header, two-column profile grid, and vertical scrolling.
**Do** use semantic theme resources and localization bindings for new native controls and copy.
**Do** retain written simulation, real read-only, local-draft, unknown-contract, stale-observation, selection, and error states alongside color.
**Do** keep normal Real startup and the Connect entry point clear, and place Mock selection under Advanced / Developer mode.
**Do** keep USB identification separate from explicit connection, use neutral USB identity, and disable Connect/Reconnect unless one safe HID candidate is identified.
**Do** use Display / Animations and color IPS in user-facing copy; retain the legacy serialized `Oled` key only for local-draft compatibility.
**Do** use the shared freshness snapshot for body and header; omit stale header battery without changing connection status.
**Do** keep the four physical-key selection regions aligned to the supplied photograph and pair blue selection with a distinct keyboard-focus ring.
**Do** keep integration evidence independent, show concrete owned changes before Apply, and retain keyboard focus and the open review through status updates.
**Do** preserve explicit service startup or its saved opt-in, native trust, metadata-only history, and session-only hardware AUTO initially off.
**Do** keep exact selected-key review, ACK acceptance, focused behavior observation and absent readback distinct; preserve K1 and the global-save warning.
**Do** show current feedback failure ahead of a historical preview result and explain reconnect or off/on recovery while retaining the saved preference.

**Do** keep static upload inert until the attested capability and exact overwrite confirmation; disclose destroyed pixels, unknown aliases and global save, and distinguish metadata success from user-observed image acceptance.
donts: **Don't** imply simulated read/write evidence represents a physical device operation.
**Don't** present a Bluetooth or USB connection or telemetry sample as configuration readback, Synced, or a verified capability contract when fields are absent.

**Don't** extend physical RGB acceptance beyond separately command-tested and user-observed 01/00 on each exact accepted USB or BLE identity and firmware; USB proof never grants BLE acceptance, and ACKs or offline images alone remain insufficient.

**Don't** add full-profile writes/readback, injected physical Test, brightness setters, firmware operations/probes, GIF uploads or other physical Display targets. Accepted selected-key, RGB and exact-scope static Display controls use separate gates; normal physical reads remain `00`/`9F`, and approval refresh uses only `00`.
**Don't** replace native WPF controls with web approximations or apply HTML/CSS detectors to this application.
**Don't** treat screenshot review as hardware, actual monitor DPI, Windows high-contrast, or screen-reader acceptance; those require separate evidence.
